name: Minimal logarithmic energy of 100 points on the sphere
description: Place 100 points on the unit sphere to minimize the logarithmic energy, the sum over all pairs of log(1/distance), the energy in Smale's 7th problem. The lowest published energy, -1083.377140539, is the putative global minimum: it is not proven minimal, but random-restart local optimisation reproduces it within seconds, so the task measures whether an optimiser reaches it.

sources.locator: Rakhmanov, Saff and Zhou (1994), Minimal discrete energy on the sphere: the minimal logarithmic and Riesz energy problems and numerical minima.
Nerattini, Brauchart and Kiessling (2014), supplement table 6.2 (s = 0): putatively minimal standardized pair energy v_0(100) = -0.21886406879576, i.e. E = -1083.377140539.

Amore, Figueroa and Ramos (2025), CC BY 4.0 dataset of local minima of the logarithmic energy; LocalMinima.zip, member 100.zip (39 minima for N = 100), whose lowest minimum reproduces the tabulated value to 2.9e-10.

evaluation.benchmark: Minimal logarithmic energy of 100 points on the sphere
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: construct() -> array of shape (N, 3) of nonzero vectors; each is normalised to the unit sphere. Score: the logarithmic energy sum_{i<j} log(1 / |x_i - x_j|) (natural logarithm, chordal distances, pair terms summed with math.fsum); minimize. Points closer than 1e-9, a wrong shape or non-finite values make the candidate invalid.

limitations: The record is the lowest published value we could check: the tables of Nerattini, Brauchart and Kiessling (2014), compiled from Rakhmanov, Saff and Zhou (1995) and Calef (2009), and the 2025 landscape survey of Amore, Figueroa and Ramos. R. Womersley's published point sets could not be accessed when the task was prepared, so a lower value in sources we could not read cannot be excluded.
Points are normalised to the unit sphere before scoring, so only directions matter; the record coordinates are public, so scores measure the returned construction, not the search that produced it.
Candidate Python runs inside the evaluator process and is trusted research code; the evaluator recomputes the score from the returned array but does not sandbox the program.

The reference is easy to reach: L-BFGS on the normalised coordinates from random starting points ties it within the 1e-9 margin in about a second (55 of 129 random starts in 35 s on one core for N = 100), no start went below it, and the 39 local minima published by Amore, Figueroa and Ramos (2025) contain no lower value. The headroom of the task is therefore the gap between the seed and this value; a score below it by more than the margin would be a new record and is not expected.

state_of_the_art.statement: The lowest published logarithmic energy we found for 100 points on the unit sphere is E = -1083.377140539 (standardized pair energy v_0 = -0.21886406879576 in the data tables of Nerattini, Brauchart and Kiessling 2014, compiled from Rakhmanov, Saff and Zhou 1995 and Calef 2009). The lowest of the 39 local minima published by Amore, Figueroa and Ramos (2025) attains it to 2.9e-10. No minimizer is proven for this N; rigorous results exist only for a few small N such as N = 6 and N = 12.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find 100 points on the unit sphere with minimal logarithmic energy (Smale's 7th problem; elliptic Fekete points).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Smale's 7th problem asks for an efficient construction of near-minimal logarithmic-energy points, which are linked to well-conditioned polynomial systems and to charged-particle models; even putative minima for moderate N are known only from extensive numerical searches.
